ourGain.point: Connection path per tripod (drop-in plate, 3/8 bolt, PE200 with two M6-16 screws, CPC center rod and lock nut) as one chooser column
Innorel RT90C plate slip: the AM5's own tapered plate does not lock in the Innorel cup; use the Innorel plate with the 3/8 screw or a three-screw adapter
Celestron CPC tripod: unscrew the center rod, run it up into the plate and lock the PE200 with the nut; a longer threaded rod is needed if the tray stays on

painPoints.pain: The TC40 is not steady enough for a C6, C8 or other heavy scope when imaging
painPoints.details: AM5 owners with SCTs find the light carbon tripod shakes; others are fine with small refractors and a loaded weight bag.

quotes.text: I have the carbon fiber tripod and it just isn't steady enough for my C6 and C8 for imaging.

painPoints.pain: A non-ZWO tripod does not bolt straight onto the AM5
painPoints.details: LiteRoc, CPC and other astronomy tripods need a 3/8-16 bolt, the center pin removed, a mini pier or the PE200.

quotes.text: You do need to get your own bolt to go up through the middle, but it's trivial purchase from a hardware store.

painPoints.pain: The AM5's own plate slips in the Innorel RT90C cup
painPoints.details: The plates look alike but the AM5 plate is tapered; one owner's mount tilted overnight.

quotes.text: Lesson learned: if you're using the Innorel tripod, use the plate supplied with the tripod.

painPoints.pain: The TC40 sits too low for visual use and low targets over trees
painPoints.details: Owners want a taller base than 800 mm without stacking extensions.

quotes.text: I like the taller height of the Literoc which makes it easier for visual use and also for me to image lower horizon objects when they get close to the tree tops.

painPoints.pain: Wind shakes a light AM5 setup and ruins subs
painPoints.details: Owners load the TC40 weight bag or move to a heavier tripod for windy sites.

quotes.text: It also does better with the rock sack loaded up.
